summary: Iteration 4 hardening + Pro tier monetization tested. Backend: 53/53 PASS (10 new iter4 + 43 regression). All new behaviors verified: like idempotency (double-like keeps count, unlike decrements, double-unlike no-op), apply re-apply cleanup (3x apply keeps wardrobe delta = 9 from-template items), palette 413 guard for >8MB base64, user shape with is_pro=false + 2 default airlines on register/me, free-tier 3rd-trip 402 with 'Free tier'/'Pro' detail and unblocked after POST /me/pro, publish gated to Pro (402 then 200), /me/airlines add (Pro-only 402→200) + delete with default backfill. Frontend: PRO badge → /pro nav verified, 'Welcome back, traveller.' headline, downgrade→upsell→re-upgrade cycle works end-to-end. Found and FIXED a HIGH-priority frontend crash on Pack tab (CARRY_ON_LIMIT_KG ReferenceError on line 230 of (tabs)/checklist.tsx — replaced with carryOnLimitKg.toFixed(1)). After fix, Pack tab renders correctly with airline picker showing selected profile and weight bar denominator '/ 7.0 kg' from selected airline.

ui_bugs.issue: ReferenceError: CARRY_ON_LIMIT_KG is not defined — Pack tab crashed with a red-screen on every render. FIXED in this iteration: replaced literal `{CARRY_ON_LIMIT_KG}` with `{carryOnLimitKg.toFixed(1)}` (the local computed from selectedAirline.max_kg already declared at line 47).

action_items: Verify the Pack-tab fix (already applied) survives a full bundle restart and on iOS/Android (only web-preview verified).

Existing test_user `test@packr.app` had its airline_profiles list overwritten to only ['IndiGo Domestic'] during prior testing — defaults (carry-on, IATA) are NOT auto-merged on login. user_public() falls back to DEFAULT_AIRLINES only when the field is empty/missing, not when partial. Consider either (a) resetting test user's airlines OR (b) merging defaults on login when missing the canonical ids. Non-blocking for spec.

Trip-create 402 inline error (red text below form) was not exercised end-to-end by playwright since test_user is Pro; backend behavior confirmed via pytest. Main agent or next iteration should validate the UI surfaces detail (vs generic 'failure').
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~715 lines — past the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into routers/ (auth, wardrobe, trips, templates, palette, me).
DEFAULT_AIRLINES is referenced inside user_public but defined a few lines later — works because DEFAULT_AIRLINES is module-level by import time, but reordering for readability would help.

user_public airline_profiles fallback uses `or DEFAULT_AIRLINES` so an EMPTY list also gets defaults — good. But once a user adds their own first airline (via /me/airlines after backfill), defaults are persisted to the DB and cannot be removed unless the canonical IDs `carry-on`/`iata` are protected (frontend already protects them in pro.tsx). Consistent.
Apply-template cleanup correctly checks `count_documents({'id': {'$ne': trip_id}, 'grid': item['id']})` before delete — good safety against shared from-template clones across trips.

Like/unlike use a separate template_likes collection keyed by (template_id, user_id). Recommend a unique compound index to enforce idempotency at DB level (currently relies on app-level find_one check, which is racy under concurrent likes by same user).

success_rate.frontend: PRO badge nav + /pro screen flow PASS. Downgrade→re-upgrade cycle PASS. Pack tab rendering PASS after applied fix. Trip-cap inline error UI not exercised on web (user is Pro).

Two open items for E1: (1) trip-create 402 UX surface — easy to verify by registering a new free user, creating 2 trips, and asserting the red error message in /onboarding/trip-create renders the backend detail string; (2) consider adding a unique index on template_likes(template_id, user_id) and merging DEFAULT_AIRLINES into legacy users at login to keep airline picker showing both carry-on + IATA after they add a custom one.
rca_of_issue: RCA — Pack tab crash. The iter4 spec replaces the hardcoded carry-on limit with a per-airline value. The dev added the `selectedAirline`, `carryOnLimitKg`, and the airline-chip strip + airline-aware computations correctly (line 47), BUT forgot to update the JSX label rendering at line 230 which still referenced the now-deleted module constant `CARRY_ON_LIMIT_KG`. Because the constant was removed from the module scope, every render of <Checklist/> threw 'CARRY_ON_LIMIT_KG is not defined' before any chip could even paint. Reproduction: login → tap PACK tab → red-screen. Mitigation applied: 1-line fix swapping the identifier to the local already-computed `carryOnLimitKg.toFixed(1)`. Verified by browser automation post-restart.
